Journey Framework Strategy Thesis

I became a Chelsea fan because of Eden Hazard.

Today, the next Eden Hazard might find you before you ever find him.

Discovery. Engagement. Participation. Loyalty. By John Gates.

Before the FYP, there was Hazard.

Eden Hazard
Player Interest

Chelsea Fan

That was my fan journey. What happens when TikTok can initiate millions of journeys like it?

The Research Question

How does TikTok's personalized short-form content environment influence sports fan discovery, engagement, participation and brand loyalty?

JG'S TAKE: Going viral is great. Creating a fan is better.

The Next Fan Framework

Discovery

First exposure to an athlete, team, sport, league or storyline.

Engagement

Watching, liking, commenting, sharing, following and searching.

Participation

Creating edits, memes, reactions, debates and fan content.

Identity

Belonging, rivalries, inside jokes, traditions and the sacred “we won.”

Loyalty

Repeat behavior, games, merch, tickets, advocacy and long-term fandom.

Congrats on the views. Now what?

Vanity Metrics

1,400,000 views
87,000 likes
6,400 shares

Actual Fandom Questions

Did they follow? Come back? Watch a game? Join the community? Buy anything? Still care six months later?

Attention does not equal loyalty.

Attention can be the beginning of loyalty, but it is not the same thing.

The $17 Hot Dog Test

Saw a video → watched another → followed → commented → joined the community → watched a game → bought a jersey → bought a ticket → paid an offensive amount of money for stadium food → still came back.

JG'S TAKE: Getting 2 million views is cool. Getting somebody to willingly pay $17 for a stadium hot dog might tell us a little more.
